title: Except those who pray
hookLine: except those constant in their prayer (70:22–23)
last: PANIC WHEN IT'S BAD, CLUTCHING WHEN IT'S GOOD.

cards: A sailboat in a storm doesn't stop the wind. What keeps it upright is underneath, out of sight: a heavy keel, the same weight in calm water and in bad.
The Qur'an has just said the human being is built anxious, tossed by bad news and good. Then one word: except. Not except those who never worry.
Not the rich, the lucky, or the calm by nature. The exception is a group of people with a keel, and the surah names what it is.

teach.b: Al-Ma'arij, verses twenty-two and twenty-three: except those who pray, al-musallin, who are constant in their prayer. The Arabic for constant is da'imun: lasting, steady, continuing.
Not those who pray beautifully, or for hours. Those who keep at it. Then the surah paints the whole person.

teach.h: A KNOWN RIGHT FOR THE ONE WHO ASKS.
teach.b: In their wealth there's a known right for the one who asks and the one who is deprived. They believe in the Day of Judgment. They're in awe of their Lord's punishment.
They guard their chastity. They keep their trusts and their promises. They stand by their testimony.
And the last item on the list, verse thirty-four: they guard their prayer.

teach.h: THE LIST BEGINS AND ENDS WITH PRAYER.
teach.b: The list begins with prayer and ends with prayer; the giving, the honesty, the kept promises sit inside it. Commentators noticed the two prayer verses aren't the same. Constant means they don't drop it.
Guarding means they look after it: its times, its conditions, its attention. A hadith in both Bukhari and Muslim fits this exactly.

teach.h: THE MOST CONSTANT, EVEN IF SMALL.
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was asked which deeds Allah loves most, and he said: the most constant, even if they're small. So in this surah, the answer to an anxious nature isn't a heroic burst of devotion.
It's steadiness: the same prayer, at the same time, in a good week and a bad one. That's the keel. It doesn't stop the weather.
It keeps the boat upright while the weather does what weather does.

how: Muslims pray the five daily prayers at set times, and scholars stress keeping them consistently; some also keep small voluntary acts every day, following the hadith that the deeds Allah loves most are the most constant, even if small.

praying for long hours through the night
steady, keeping at prayer day after day

games.q: you want to answer your anxious nature the way 70:22–23 describes. which plan fits the verse?
o: one long night of prayer a month.
a small prayer kept every day.
games.why: da'imun: constant. the hadith says the deeds Allah loves most are the most constant, even if small.

practice: If you pray, choose one daily prayer you most often miss or rush and decide to keep it on time this week; if you don't, choose two minutes of quiet at the same time each day.
Picture that moment tomorrow: where you are, what time it is, what usually gets in the way. See yourself keeping it anyway.

wordCard.voice: Da'imun. In 70:22–23 those who pray, al-musallin, are da'imun, constant: not spectacular, but steady, lasting, continuing. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, 70:23: constant in their prayer. da'im, lasting, continuing.

carryVoice: Your line: constant in prayer. Small and steady, in good weeks and bad, still counts. Day six hundred forty-seven, done.
